I still see HDDs being a thing though. With SSDs you can only write to them so many times before they stop working. So for recording videos, an HDD is still ideal.

Not really. SSDs can now endure ~1 petabyte of writing before they fail. That's almost a year of compressed 4k video being written to the drive before failure. For comparison, a HDD would need to be in operation writing at max speed for 116 days straight before it wrote the equivalent amount of data as a failing SSD.

An SSD will practically last for as long as you'll need it, regardless of how you use it. By the time you've worn it down, drives would be much cheaper, faster, and larger and you'll probably be wanting an upgrade anyways.

I'm looking to rebuild my gaming computer next year once AMD comes out with their Zen processor assuming it lives up to their marketing/hype. I like Intel's speed, but I've never been able to justify their price:performance ratio. Same with SSDs. If this article pans out, I may put together my first PC that's purely SSD.
